title: Give a Function the Full Situation
content:
What problem does this solve?
One parameter is enough for a single clue. Dispatch decisions often need several facts at once: a destination and a status, a price and a quantity, or a party, supplies, and a warning flag. Multiple parameters let the call site hand over the whole situation without leaning on global variables.

Previously in your program
You wrote functions like inspect_clue(clue) and antidote_count(stock) with one input. Now the parameter list can describe every value the decision needs.

Basic syntax
  def route_label(destination, status):
      return f"{destination}: {status}"

  print(route_label("Gloamfen", "Review"))

What actually happens
Parameters bind by position unless you later use keyword arguments. In route_label("Gloamfen", "Review"), destination receives "Gloamfen" and status receives "Review". Swap the arguments and the meaning swaps too. A function can also receive lists as parameters and work from those values instead of hidden globals.

When this is useful
Add another parameter when the function needs another independent fact to decide or build its result.
concepts: A function can declare multiple parameters
Positional arguments bind in order to those parameters
Collection parameters let a function work without global data

examples.title: Two inputs, one label
examples.explanation: The first argument fills destination; the second fills status.

examples.title: Lists as parameters
examples.explanation: The list arrives through the parameter. The function does not need a global party variable.

common_mistakes: Swapping arguments at the call site so names and roles trade places
Trying to fake multiple inputs with *args when named parameters are the objective
Hardcoding a return value instead of using every parameter
Relying on global lists when the function should receive them as parameters

exercises.title: Two inputs bind in order
hints: Match arguments to parameters left to right.
destination becomes Gloamfen; status becomes Review.
The returned string is Gloamfen: Review.

exercises.title: Name both parameters
exercises.prompt: Fill in the parameter list so supply_cost can multiply price by quantity when called as supply_cost(5, 3).
hints: The body uses two names: price and quantity.
Those names must appear in the def header.

tests.message: supply_cost must multiply its two parameters.

exercises.title: Swapped at the call site
exercises.prompt: The function is fine, but the call passes role and name in the wrong order. Fix the call so it prints Mira — Scout.
hints: name should receive Mira; role should receive Scout.

tests.message: Keep badge(name, role) working for other inputs.

exercises.title: Carry capacity
exercises.prompt: Write carry_capacity(base_slots, bonus_slots) that returns the sum of the two values. Accept ordinary totals, zero bonuses, and negative adjustments.
hints: Both inputs are numbers the caller provides.
Combine them with addition (or an equivalent calculation).

tests.message: A zero bonus should leave the base unchanged.
Negative adjustments must reduce the total.

exercises.title: Dispatch status
exercises.prompt:
Write dispatch_status(party, supplies, warning_active) that returns:
- "Denied" when warning_active is True or party is empty
- otherwise "Ready" when supplies has at least two items per party member
- otherwise "Review"

Use the three parameters to make the whole decision. Do not print.
exercises.success_message: Status decided from the full situation — party, supplies, and warning together.
hints: Check denial conditions first: an active warning or an empty party.
Ready means len(supplies) is at least twice len(party).
Use if / elif / else (or equivalent) and return one of the three strings.

tests.message: Use len(...) inside dispatch_status when measuring party or supplies.
An empty party must be Denied.
One member with two supplies should be Ready.
Two members with only three supplies should be Review.
An active warning must Deny even when supplies look fine.
Two members with four supplies should be Ready.
